summary: All four blocks keep the events, objects, negation and the causal order of the English; the present tense, the emphasis on the addressee and the dry narrator are intact. One register drift: 'eminent' became 'beroemde' (famous), which asserts public fame the narrator does not claim.

comprehension.q: What covers the walls of the room, and where have the books ended up beyond the bookcases?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Tegen elke centimeter muur staat een boekenkast met zes planken tot bijna aan het plafond; de boeken stromen over op de tafels en de banken en maken kleine stapels onder de ramen.

comprehension.q: Why is the back row of paperbacks standing on old tissue boxes or pieces of wood?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: De achterste rij staat hoger, zodat je de achterste boeken boven de voorste boeken kunt zien.

comprehension.q: Whose living room is this, and how is Harry related to the couple?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Het huis van professor Michael Verres-Evans en zijn vrouw Petunia Evans-Verres; Harry James Potter-Evans-Verres is hun adoptiezoon.

comprehension.q: What lies on the living-room table, and what is unusual about the envelope?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Een brief en een envelop van geelachtig perkament zonder postzegel; op de envelop staat in smaragdgroene inkt 'de heer H. Potter'.

comprehension.q: How are the Professor and his wife arguing, and why are they not shouting?
comprehension.answer_from_nl: Ze praten op scherpe toon tegen elkaar maar schreeuwen niet; de professor vindt schreeuwen onbeschaafd.

findings.problem: 'eminent' (distinguished, respected in his field) has become 'beroemde' (famous), a claim of public fame the narrator does not make; the mock-formal label is also flattened into an ordinary compliment.
findings.evidence: EN: 'the eminent Professor Michael Verres-Evans' vs NL: 'de beroemde professor Michael Verres-Evans'
findings.required_fix: Use a word that means distinguished/respected rather than famous, e.g. 'de eminente professor' (glossed, as s02 and s03 do) or 'de vooraanstaande professor'; do not assert fame.

findings.problem: The narrator's capitalised label 'The Professor' (Michael's nickname in the narration) is rendered lowercase, losing the small mock-title the bible asks to keep.
findings.evidence: EN: 'The Professor and his wife … The Professor considers shouting' vs NL: 'De professor en zijn vrouw … De professor vindt'; bible: 'Exception: de Professor (capital P) when the narrator uses it as Michael's label.'
findings.required_fix: Write 'De Professor' (capital P) in both sentences of b014, as in s02/s03; keep lowercase 'professor' before the name in b012.

findings.problem: 'stacked to the brim' is reduced to plain fullness; the overflowing-container image that prepares 'And it still isn't enough' is gone.
findings.evidence: EN: 'stacked to the brim with hardback books' vs NL: 'staan helemaal vol boeken met een harde kaft'
findings.required_fix: Optional: restore the brim image if a plain form is available ('tot de rand toe vol'); otherwise accept.

findings.fragment: maken kleine stapels onder de ramen
findings.problem: 'little heaps' are untidy piles; 'stapels' suggests orderly stacks, slightly tidying the chaos the paragraph describes.
findings.evidence: EN: 'making little heaps under the windows' vs NL: 'maken kleine stapels onder de ramen'
findings.required_fix: Optional: 'kleine hoopjes' or 'kleine hopen' would keep the disorder; 'stapels' is acceptable.
